work.title: Resolve a stage's skill composition deterministically
work.description: Turn declared manifests into one resolved composition for a stage: exactly one stage skill, required and recommended dependencies, conflict refusal, capability requirements, deterministic ordering, and a resolution digest that is a pure function of the resolved set. Resolution is a read — it reports the selection and the reason for every inclusion and every omission, and writes nothing. Precedence is fixed here: Core invariants, Work state, and repository policy outrank any skill; a secondary skill may add method and may never alter lifecycle decisions or return rules.
acceptance: Resolving a stage yields exactly one stage skill, or refuses with a named error when zero or several would apply
Required dependencies resolve, recommended ones are included or reported as omitted with a reason, and a declared conflict or an unmet capability refuses the resolution
The same inputs always produce the same order and the same resolution digest, and any change to a resolved skill's content changes that digest
A CLI read prints the resolved composition with a reason per included and per omitted skill, and mutates nothing

result.summary: Resolution is a new pure core module: resolveComposition(stage, manifests, hostCapabilities) selects the one stage skill by the codepatrol-<stage> id convention, closes over required dependencies, includes or omits recommended ones with reasons, refuses on conflicts (SKILL_CONFLICT), unmet capabilities (SKILL_CAPABILITY_UNMET), and zero/several stage matches (SKILL_UNRESOLVABLE), and emits a deterministic order plus a sha256 resolution digest of the resolved set. Manifests gain optional requires/recommends/conflicts under schemaVersion 1; `codepatrol skill resolve <stage>` prints the composition with per-skill reasons and mutates nothing.
result.handoff:
# Plan: Resolve a stage's skill composition deterministically (INIT-1.2)

## Finding (P1)
INIT-1.1 is on main: src/core/skill.ts (schemaVersion 1, strict parser over id/version/kind/capabilities/digest) and `codepatrol skill list` verifying all seven manifests. The manifest declares no dependencies or conflicts yet — this Work adds them additively under schemaVersion 1, so a manifest without the new fields still parses (the "additive later" rule INIT-1.1 set). Core stays filesystem-free; the CLI already owns the skills read via listShippedSkills.

## Product files Build touches
1. src/core/skill.ts — extend SkillManifest, parser, and serializer with optional `requires`, `recommends`, `conflicts`: arrays of unique skill-id tokens (SKILL_ID), each defaulting to absent. schemaVersion stays 1.
2. src/core/skill-resolution.ts (new) — the pure resolver and its types/errors.
3. src/cli/commands/skill.ts — add `skill resolve <stage>` to the existing command.
4. skills/codepatrol-{plan,review,build,verify,ship}/skill.json — add `recommends: ["codepatrol-work"]` (digests are over SKILL.md, so they are unchanged). spec/work manifests unchanged.
5. src/test/skill-resolution.test.ts (new); parser additions covered in src/test/skill.test.ts.

## Resolver (src/core/skill-resolution.ts)
```ts
resolveComposition(stage: Stage, manifests: readonly SkillManifest[], hostCapabilities: readonly string[]): SkillComposition
```
- **Stage selection**: the stage skill is the manifest whose id is `codepatrol-${stage}` (convention, not a new field — nothing to drift). Zero matches or several matches refuse with CodepatrolError SKILL_UNRESOLVABLE naming the stage and the offending count.
- **Closure**: start from the stage skill; iterate to a fixpoint over sorted ids — requires of every included skill must be in the available manifests (a missing required id refuses SKILL_UNRESOLVABLE naming both ends); recommends are included when available, omitted otherwise and reported with the reason "recommended by <id>, not available".
- **Conflicts**: an included skill whose `conflicts` names another included skill refuses SKILL_CONFLICT naming both.
- **Capabilities**: every capability of every included skill must appear in hostCapabilities, else SKILL_CAPABILITY_UNMET naming the skill and the capability.
- **Order**: the stage skill first, then secondaries sorted by id. Fixed forever.
- **Digest**: sha256 over the canonical JSON of `[{ id, version, digest }]` in that order — a pure function of the resolved set, so identical inputs give identical output and any change to a resolved skill's recorded digest changes the resolution digest.
- Output: `{ stage, skills: [{ id, version, kind, digest }] (ordered), digest, included: [{ id, reason }], omitted: [{ id, reason }] }`. Reasons: "the stage skill for <stage>", "required by <id>", "recommended by <id>".
- The precedence rule from the Work text — Core invariants, Work state, and repository policy outrank any skill; a secondary may add method and never alter lifecycle decisions or return rules — is stated in the module's doc comment. Resolution is selection, not governance.

## CLI read (`codepatrol skill resolve <stage>`)
- Validates the stage argument against STAGES (unknown stage → INVALID_ARGUMENT with usage).
- Resolves over listShippedSkills (package-relative, as today) with the host capabilities the CLI provides: a named constant `HOST_CAPABILITIES = ["cli"]` in the command module — the one capability this host truthfully offers.
- Prints the full composition JSON including per-inclusion and per-omission reasons; mutates nothing; needs no workspace or remote. `skill list` output is unchanged.

## Tests
src/test/skill-resolution.test.ts:
- exactly one stage skill resolves; zero and several each refuse SKILL_UNRESOLVABLE (acceptance 1).
- required dependencies resolve transitively; a missing required id refuses; a recommended skill is included with its reason or reported omitted with its reason; a declared conflict refuses SKILL_CONFLICT; an unmet capability refuses SKILL_CAPABILITY_UNMET (acceptance 2).
- same inputs twice → identical order and digest; mutating one skill's digest changes the resolution digest (acceptance 3).
- CLI: `skill resolve plan` prints the composition with reasons for codepatrol-plan and the included codepatrol-work, is sorted and idempotent, and an unknown stage refuses (acceptance 4).
src/test/skill.test.ts (extended): parser accepts the new optional fields, refuses duplicates inside them, refuses non-skill-id tokens, and a manifest without them still parses.

## Acceptance coverage
1. Exactly one stage skill or named refusal — id-convention selection + SKILL_UNRESOLVABLE tests.
2. Requires resolve, recommends included/omitted with reason, conflict/unmet capability refuse — closure + error tests.
3. Deterministic order and digest, content-sensitive — digest tests.
4. CLI read with reasons, mutating nothing — `skill resolve <stage>` + CLI test.

## Verification for Build
npm run verify (typecheck, unit tests, smoke, --help showing skill resolve).

## Non-goals
No recording of compositions on runs (INIT-1.4), no evaluation harness (INIT-1.3), no telemetry. No new capability tokens beyond "cli". No precedence enforcement mechanism — documentation only, as the Work fixes precedence in prose here.

# Review Report — INIT-1.2 Resolve a stage's skill composition deterministically

The plan is approved.

## Completeness (R1)
Each acceptance criterion maps to one or more named tests:
1. Exactly one stage skill or named refusal → zero/exactly-one/several stage skill cases asserting SKILL_UNRESOLVABLE.
2. Requires/recommends/conflict/unmet-capability behavior → transitive requires, missing required, recommended-included-with-reason, recommended-omitted-with-reason, SKILL_CONFLICT, SKILL_CAPABILITY_UNMET.
3. Determinism and content-sensitive digest → same-input-twice test plus digest-sensitivity test where one resolved skill's digest changes the resolution digest.
4. CLI read with reasons → `skill resolve plan` prints the composition with reasons and refuses an unknown stage; mutates nothing.

Task dependencies form a DAG (P1 inspect → P2 design → P3 CLI → P4 plan → P5 complete). Every task names its file set; blast radius = union of those files. Verification is `npm run verify` (typecheck, unit tests, smoke, `--help` listing `skill resolve`).

## Reference validation (R2)
- `src/core/skill.ts` exports `SKILL_SCHEMA_VERSION`, `SKILL_TYPE`, `SKILL_KINDS`, `parseSkillManifest`, `serializeSkillManifest`, `skillContentDigest`. The strict v1 parser is the additive extension target.
- `src/core/identifiers.ts` exports `SKILL_ID = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/` — the right regex for the new arrays.
- `src/core/types.ts` exports `STAGES = ['plan','review','build','verify','ship']` and `STAGE_ROLES`; the `codepatrol-${stage}` convention matches the existing shipped ids with no STAGES change.
- `src/core/json.ts` exports `sha256` for the resolution digest.
- `src/cli/commands/skill.ts` already hosts `skill list` and `listShippedSkills`; the new `resolve` action slots in without registry edits.
- `src/test/skill.test.ts` already covers round-trip, unknown-field, value, capabilities, and the shipped-manifests integrity test; adding requires/recommends/conflicts cases is contained.
- SKILL.md-only digests (verified in `skillContentDigest`) keep the shipped-manifests integrity test green when skill.json gains new fields.

## Risks noted
- The id-convention stage selection is safe for the current seven shipped skills; a doc-comment in `skill-resolution.ts` documenting the rule is the right place to call it out, and the plan already commits to it.
- Host capabilities stay at `["cli"]` — no new tokens invented. The precedence prose in the module's doc comment covers the Work's stated rule without inventing enforcement machinery.
- INIT-1.3 (evaluation harness) and INIT-1.4 (recording compositions on runs) are explicitly non-goals; the four acceptance criteria do not require them.

## Cited evidence
- Plan handoff: see `availableResults[0].handoff` in the Review v1 handoff.
- Plan traces (observation + two decisions): see the `plan` attempt's `traces` in the v1 handoff.
- Plan task outcomes (P1–P5 completed with notes): see the `plan` attempt's `result.todo` in the v1 handoff.
- Review traces (R1 plan-completeness observation, R2 reference-validation observation): see this Review attempt's `traces`.

## Verdict
Continue. The plan is decision-complete. There is nothing to return to Plan for.

result.handoff:
# Build: Resolve a stage's skill composition deterministically (INIT-1.2)

## What changed
- src/core/skill.ts — SkillManifest gains optional `requires`, `recommends`, `conflicts`: arrays of unique skill-id tokens (`SKILL_ID`), each defaulting to absent. The parser enforces the additive extension under schemaVersion 1: a manifest without the new fields still parses; manifests with the new fields are validated (arrays of well-formed skill ids, unique per array). The serializer includes each field when present and omits it when undefined, so the byte representation of a manifest without the new fields is unchanged.
- src/core/skill-resolution.ts (new) — the pure resolver. `resolveComposition(stage, manifests, hostCapabilities)` returns `{ stage, skills, digest, included, omitted }`. Stage selection by `codepatrol-${stage}` id convention. Closure over requires with smallest-id source as the recorded reason. Recommends walk in id order; an available skill joins with reason `recommended by <id>`, an unavailable one lands in `omitted` with reason `recommended by <id>, not available`. Order is stage skill first, then secondaries in ascending id. Digest is sha256 over the canonical JSON of `[{ id, version, digest }]`. Refusals: SKILL_UNRESOLVABLE (zero/several stage matches, missing required id, self-required id), SKILL_CONFLICT (declared conflict between two included skills), SKILL_CAPABILITY_UNMET (an included skill's capability absent from hostCapabilities). Module doc-comment states the precedence rule from the Work text: resolution is selection, not governance.
- src/cli/commands/skill.ts — `skill resolve <stage>` action added to the existing CommandSpec. Validates the stage against STAGES, resolves over `listShippedSkills(shippedSkillsDirectory)` with `HOST_CAPABILITIES = ['cli']`, prints the composition JSON. The action mutates nothing and does not need a workspace. Usage text updated to include `skill resolve <stage>`.
- skills/codepatrol-{plan,review,build,verify,ship}/skill.json — each gains `recommends: ["codepatrol-work"]`. The five stage skills now resolve to themselves plus codepatrol-work. skills/codepatrol-spec/skill.json and skills/codepatrol-work/skill.json are unchanged. SKILL.md files unchanged → recorded `digest` field is unchanged → `every shipped skill carries a manifest that parses and reproduces` test stays green.
- src/test/skill.test.ts — extended with parser tests for absent requires/recommends/conflicts, well-formed arrays, non-skill-id token refusal, duplicate entry refusal, and non-array value refusal. New CLI tests: `skill resolve plan` prints the composition with reasons and is idempotent (calling it twice returns the same JSON), refuses an unknown stage, and refuses missing or extra positional arguments.
- src/test/skill-resolution.test.ts (new) — 12 tests covering each acceptance criterion: exactly one stage skill / zero / several / transitive requires / missing required / self-required / recommended-included-with-reason / recommended-absent-omitted / declared conflict / unmet capability / same-inputs-determinism and digest-sensitivity / stage-first ordering.

## Validation
- npm run typecheck: clean.
- npm test: 280/280 pass (12 new resolver tests + 5 new parser tests + 3 new CLI tests).
- npm run smoke: pass.
- node bin/codepatrol.js --help: lists `skill resolve <stage>`.
- node bin/codepatrol.js skill resolve plan: returns the composition with stage skill first and codepatrol-work second.
- node bin/codepatrol.js skill resolve nope: refuses with INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the unknown stage.
- Candidate commit 51bb15ee36017fae072889493c13ae9f3a0300ad is on refs/heads/codepatrol/work/INIT-1.2-resolve-a-stage-s-skill-composition-deterministi; the worktree is clean.

## Acceptance evidence
1. Exactly one stage skill or named refusal — zero/several stage skill tests, single stage skill test.
2. Requires/recommends/conflict/unmet capability behavior — transitive requires, missing required, recommended-included-with-reason, recommended-omitted, SKILL_CONFLICT, SKILL_CAPABILITY_UNMET.
3. Deterministic order and digest, content-sensitive — same-inputs-twice test plus digest-sensitivity test (changing a resolved skill's digest changes the composition digest).
4. CLI read with reasons, mutating nothing — `skill resolve plan` test asserts idempotence and the reasons array; an unknown stage test asserts the refusal; the CLI uses `listShippedSkills` with no workspace and no remote.
